questions.stem: Element X is in Group 2, Period 4 of the periodic table. Which prediction about its properties is most accurate?

options.text: It will be a non-metal that forms X²⁻ ions
It will be a reactive metal that forms X²⁺ ions and reacts with water
It will be an unreactive gas with a full outer shell
It will be a liquid halogen at room temperature

questions.explanation: Group 2 elements (alkaline earth metals) have 2 outer electrons, which they lose to form 2+ ions. Being in Period 4 means it has 4 electron shells — this element is calcium. Like other Group 2 metals, it reacts with water (though less vigorously than Group 1 metals) to form a hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.stem: The melting points of Group 7 elements are: F₂ = -220°C, Cl₂ = -101°C, Br₂ = -7°C, I₂ = 114°C. Predict the approximate melting point of astatine (At₂).

options.text: About -300°C
About 0°C
About 200-350°C
About 1000°C

questions.explanation: Melting points increase going down Group 7 due to increasing London dispersion forces. The increases between successive elements are roughly 119°C, 94°C, and 121°C. Continuing this trend, astatine's melting point would be approximately 200-350°C above iodine's. The accepted estimate is around 302°C.

questions.stem: A newly discovered element Z has the electronic configuration 2,8,8,8,1. Based on this, which set of properties would you predict?

options.text: High melting point, forms coloured compounds, acts as a catalyst
Soft metal, low density, very reactive with water, stored under oil
Yellow-green gas, toxic, forms negative ions
Colourless gas, completely unreactive

questions.explanation: With 1 electron in its outer shell, element Z is in Group 1 (alkali metals). Group 1 metals are soft, have low densities, and are highly reactive with water. Being in Period 5 (5 shells), it would be more reactive than potassium. These properties match rubidium, which must be stored under oil to prevent reaction with air and moisture.

questions.stem: Strontium (Sr) is in Group 2, between calcium (above) and barium (below). Calcium reacts steadily with water, while barium reacts vigorously. How would strontium react with water?

options.text: It would not react with water at all
It would react less vigorously than calcium
It would react more vigorously than calcium but less vigorously than barium
It would react more vigorously than barium

questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down Group 2 (same as Group 1) because the outer electrons are further from the nucleus and easier to lose. Since strontium is between calcium and barium, its reactivity with water will be intermediate — more vigorous than calcium but less vigorous than barium.

questions.stem: An unknown element forms an ionic compound with chlorine that has the formula XCl₂. The element also forms a basic oxide. Which part of the periodic table is this element most likely from?

options.text: Group 1, since it forms ionic compounds
Group 7, since it reacts with chlorine
Group 2, since XCl₂ suggests a 2+ charge and its oxide is basic
Group 0, since noble gases are very stable

questions.explanation: The formula XCl₂ indicates that X has a valency of 2, forming X²⁺ ions (each Cl⁻ needs one positive charge, and there are two chlorines). Forming basic oxides is characteristic of metals. Group 2 metals have 2 outer electrons, form 2+ ions, and produce basic oxides — all matching the description.
